Why go: two days in Ang Thong with a park bungalow

The national park bungalows on Koh Wua Talab (Wua Ta Lap) are the only indoor rooms inside Ang Thong Marine Park, and there are very few of them. They are allocated by the park, and the park's own online booking system has been unreliable in the 2026 season. We book the bungalow for you as part of the trip, so you don't need to deal with the park office, phone queues or room rates: we take care of everything, from the boat to the room.

Staying overnight means you see the park after 15:30, when the last day boats leave. Watch the sunset from the beach or the viewpoint, eat at the park restaurant, sleep with the sound of the sea, and have the reefs and kayaking to yourselves on the second morning before the day boats arrive around 10:00. Day one follows the speedboat route: the Emerald Lake on Koh Mae Ko (15–20 minutes up steep wooden steps to the platform above the Thale Nai lagoon), then kayaking, snorkelling and lunch around Koh Wua Talab. On day two you can climb the 500 m viewpoint trail at dawn (sunrise is about 06:00 from May to October and 06:30–06:40 from January to March) or walk to the quieter west-side beach. The return boat leaves around 15:00 and you are back on Koh Samui at 16:00–16:30.

The bungalow is simple: beds, a fan, bed linen and towels, with no air-conditioning and no hot water. Electricity runs until 21:00. The bathroom and toilet are kept very clean, which is the main thing guests ask us about. Compared with the tent version (3,600 THB), the bungalow costs 600 THB more per adult for a proper bed, walls and a door.

Who this tour is for

  • Couples and families who want the empty-park experience without sleeping in a tent.
  • Travellers who want everything arranged, including the hard-to-get park room.
  • Photographers after sunset and dawn light on the islands.
  • Families with children: children aged 3–11 pay the child price, infants up to 2 travel free, and a room is easier with kids than a tent.

Who should choose another tour

  • Happy to camp and want to save 600 THB per adult: the tent trip.
  • Need air-conditioning, hot water or a resort standard: a VIP day tour and a night back on Samui.
  • Only have one day: the speedboat day tour.
  • Your own group and timing: the private speedboat (day only).
  • Pregnant or with back problems: both crossings are by speedboat over open sea; we don't advise it.

What to bring

  • A torch or head torch for the walk down after sunset and the dawn climb.
  • Insect repellent and a light long-sleeved layer for the evening.
  • A change of clothes and toiletries (towels and bed linen are provided).
  • A power bank: electricity runs until 21:00 and Wi-Fi is limited.
  • Reef-safe sunscreen, a hat and shoes with grip.
  • Cash in Thai baht for the park fee (300 THB per foreign adult, 150 THB per child aged 3–14) and for drinks or anything at the park restaurant not covered by your package.
  • Personal medication and snacks: there are no shops on the island.

Good to know

  • Season: the park is closed every year 1 November–15 December; the bungalow trip runs from 16 December to 31 October. February to April has the calmest sea; May to September is good most days; October is wetter. December to February is peak season and bungalows are very limited, so book as early as you can.
  • Weather on day two: the captain decides when it is safe to cross, and strong wind can delay the return, so keep the afternoon and evening of day two free of flights and ferries. If we cancel before departure for weather, you choose a full refund or a new date.
  • Evening routine: come down from the viewpoint before dark with a torch. The park restaurant serves dinner 18:00–19:00 and closes at 19:00.
  • Park rules: no alcohol is sold in the park, fires are not allowed, no swimming in the Emerald Lake, and keep food away from the monkeys. Keep noise down after the electricity goes off at 21:00.
  • Wildlife: dusky langurs and long-tailed macaques live around the headquarters. Close windows and doors when you go out.
  • Mobility: bungalows are near the beach; the viewpoint trail is steep with ropes and is optional.
  • Children: children's life jackets are always on board and children wear them at all times on the boat.
  • Drones: need prior Department of National Parks permission plus CAAT/NBTC registration.
  • Booking: confirmation is by email and WhatsApp after payment, once the bungalow is secured. Tell us your group size so we can allocate the right room, and have passport numbers ready for the accident insurance.

Pickup and meeting point

Hotel transfers on both days are included from the main areas of Koh Samui: Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam, Choeng Mon, Bang Rak and Plai Laem. Remote areas (Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao, Thong Krut and similar) cost 400 THB per person return. Day-one pickup is 07:30–08:30, with check-in at the pier at 08:30–08:45. Your exact time and the pier location come by email and WhatsApp the day before. This trip departs from Koh Samui only. Pack a small overnight bag and leave the rest at your hotel.
